perform.line:
/explain Why is a language model checked on text it was not trained on, and how do these lines cut the one long string into a training piece and a validation piece? Show it on the 1,115,394-character Shakespeare text: the first 90% of characters train, the last 10% are held back.
The reader already knows: the corpus is one string, its length is counted, and characters map to ints.
Do not cover: why validation text must stay unseen.
Afterwards the reader should be able to: say the first 90% of characters train and the last 10% validate.

out.lead:
You can now turn any string into ids and back. Before the script encodes anything, it cuts the one long string in two.

A language model can memorize its text. A score on text it already studied would not show whether it learned anything general. So the script holds back a small piece to check on later. Lines 37-40 make that cut.
